blocks.text: After you create a user portal for your organization, you can add links to any applications that your employees and partners are authorized to access.
User portal links provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Allow users to view the private applications they've been granted access to from access policies. The applications can be accessed via Browser Access, Zero Trust Browser, or Zscaler Client Connector.
Provide users a list of static links that they can access from a single user portal, such as providing access to the HR system or payroll application.

blocks.text: There are two types of links you can add to your user portals:

blocks.item: Web: Users can view and click these links to launch an application. This includes Browser Access-enabled applications, web applications set up for Zscaler Client Connector access, and public Software as a Service (SaaS) websites.

Display: Users can view these links, but they cannot click them to launch the application in a browser. These links are associated with internal applications that can only be accessed using Zscaler Client Connector.

blocks.text: If a user is connecting to Private Access (ZPA) via Zscaler Client Connector, then they see links for applications that they have access to from all devices that are currently connected to Private Access. However, an access policy can restrict access to an application based upon rule criteria.

For example, you can have an access policy rule that allows a user to access the HR application on their Windows device, but have another rule that allows them to access the sales application on their macOS device (taking into consideration device posture and trusted networks for this device). In this example, the user sees links for the HR application and sales application on the user portal, but they can only access an application if they are using the proper device. To learn more, see About Access Policy and About Device Posture Profiles.
On the Portal Links page (Zero Trust Browser > Web Access > Portal Links), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of applied filters available from the current and previous user sessions. Applied filters must be saved to the user session first before they can be viewed. Use the drop-down menu to select the applied filters to view. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Hide the filters on the page by clicking Hide Filters. Click Show Filters to display the filters.
Refresh the Portal Links page to reflect the most current information.

Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. You can also save applied filters to your preferences so that they're visible in future user sessions. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Add links to a user portal.
Filter the table to show links for a specific user portal. By default, all available links are displayed.
Expand all of the rows in the table to see more information about each portal link.
View a list of all portal links that were configured. For each link, you can see:
Name: The name of the portal link. When expanded, you can see:
User Portals: The URL for the user portal the link is displayed on.
Description: The description for the link, if available.
Logo/Favicon: The logo or favicon for the link, if available.
Display on Portal: Whether the portal link is enabled and displayed on a user portal.
URL: The user portal name.
Copy a portal link configuration to create a new link.
Edit a portal link.
Delete a portal link.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
